observations:
Torah LM2 #51 is a two-sentence teaching with no bechina language whatsoever. The criterion for proposing new packages requires 3 or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text forming an independent domain. That threshold is not met here.

The teaching presents a single causal principle in two parallel applications:
1. Resisting the yetzer hara (Evil Inclination) with stubborn resolve → yetzer hara departs
2. Ignoring distracting thoughts during prayer with resolve → thoughts depart

The second case is introduced with 'ממש כנ"ל' (exactly as above), signaling structural analogy between the two situations, not a bechina identification of their shared essence. This is best understood as a single eitza pattern applied twice — a technique the Rebbe uses to teach that the same inner posture (חזק בדעתו — firm in one's mind) operates identically whether facing the yetzer hara directly or its manifestation as prayer-disrupting thoughts.

No explicit bechina equating formulas appear in the source text. No new packages can be proposed.
